name: Intermediolateral cell column
summary: The lateral horn of gray matter present from T1 to L2, containing the preganglionic sympathetic neurons of the whole body, and its sacral counterpart at S2–S4 containing the preganglionic parasympathetic neurons for the pelvic organs. Its axons leave in the ventral roots (white rami communicantes) to the sympathetic chain. Because all sympathetic outflow to the head passes through the upper thoracic segments and the cervical cord above them, cervical and upper thoracic cord lesions cause Horner syndrome, and lesions above T6 disconnect most of the sympathetic outflow from the brain, producing autonomic dysreflexia.

anatomy.location: Lateral projection of the gray matter between the anterior and posterior horns at T1–L2 (sympathetic) and the equivalent position at S2–S4 (parasympathetic, sacral autonomic nucleus).

subdivisions.name: T1–T2 (ciliospinal center of Budge)
subdivisions.note: oculosympathetic outflow to the pupil, lid and face

subdivisions.name: T5–L2
subdivisions.note: abdominal and pelvic viscera, lower limb

afferents.via: descending autonomic fibers in the lateral funiculus

function: Preganglionic autonomic outflow: sympathetic control of blood pressure, heart rate, sweating, pupils and visceral function; sacral parasympathetic control of micturition, defecation and sexual function.

bestView.label: lateral gray region (the upper cervical cord shown carries the descending sympathetic fibers rather than the column itself)

imaging.normalAppearance: Not resolved on MRI; the descending sympathetic fibers in the cervical cord run in the lateral funiculus. Thoracic cord lesions involving the lateral gray are inferred from autonomic signs.

pathology.pathology: Cervicothoracic cord lesion with Horner syndrome
pathology.finding: Cervical or upper thoracic intramedullary lesion (syrinx, tumor, myelitis) with ipsilateral Horner syndrome.

pathology.pathology: High cord injury with autonomic dysreflexia
pathology.finding: Cord injury above T6; the syndrome is clinical.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Sagittal and axial T2 of the cervical and thoracic cord

lesionEffects.mechanism: Ciliospinal center at C8–T2 or the descending fibers above it

lesionEffects.deficit: Autonomic dysreflexia: paroxysmal hypertension, headache, flushing above the level, bradycardia
lesionEffects.mechanism: Unopposed sympathetic reflexes below a lesion above T6
Sacral parasympathetic nucleus or conus lesion

examination: Pupils and ptosis; sweating pattern of the face
Skin temperature and color below the level
Bladder and bowel history; anal tone and bulbocavernosus reflex
pearls: Horner syndrome with arm weakness and hand wasting: think of the C8–T1 region (syrinx, Pancoast tumor, cord lesion)
Severe headache with hypertension in a tetraplegic patient is autonomic dysreflexia: find the noxious trigger (full bladder) first
